classification.difficultyReason: Convert annual interest and duration to monthly periods, use two table factors, and compare interest for equal total contributions.

inlines.text: Grant can save $12000 a year and has a choice of investing it in these two ways:
$12000 annually over 5 years at 6% p.a. compounded annually.
$1000 monthly over 5 years at 6% p.a. compounded monthly.

Which option gives him more money at the end of the 5 years, and what is the difference in interest earned? Give monetary answers to the nearest cent. Use these future-value-of-$1 annuity table entries, for payments at the end of each period: 5 periods at 6% per period: 5.6371; 60 periods at 0.5% per period: 69.7700.

answer.short: The second option gives more money: $\$69770.00$ compared with $\$67645.20$. The difference in interest earned is $\$2124.80$.
answer.worked:
Option 1: $n=5$ and $r=6\%$ per year. The table factor is $5.6371$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_1&=5.6371\times12000\\&=\$67645.20\\I_1&=67645.20-12000\times5\\&=\$7645.20\end{align*}$$
Option 2: $n=5\times12=60$ and $r=6\%\div12=0.5\%$ per month. The table factor is $69.7700$.
$$\begin{align*}FV_2&=69.7700\times1000\\&=\$69770.00\\I_2&=69770.00-1000\times60\\&=\$9770.00\end{align*}$$
Both options contribute $\$60000$ in total.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Difference in interest}&=9770.00-7645.20\\&=\$2124.80\end{align*}$$
The second option gives Grant more money.
